target_customer: Students and early career tech job seekers who pay a share of income after they land a job
problem: Job seekers struggle to prepare for tech interviews and navigate hiring, and cannot afford upfront coaching fees.
business_model: Income share agreement: weekly mentorship and job search tools, with payment only after hire, financed through Leif

founders.name: Kevin Wu
education: UC Berkeley, dropped out in 2014 and later returned to finish
founders.background_notes: EdSurge 2018 gives his age as 23 and these details. Technical status not stated.

founders.name: Derrick Mar
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by EdSurge 2018, the Springshare FAQ and press coverage. The YC page does not list him.

founders.name: Evan Limanto
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page only; no other source names him.

exit.reason: Springshare says Pathrise features move into CareerShift and direct to consumer services end at the end of 2025; no reason for the deal is stated

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly a coaching operation with workflow software and job search automation, standard engineering. The harder parts were operations and ISA financing.

defensibility.rationale: Coaching and ISAs could be copied, and the financing arrangement with Leif was not exclusive of rivals in any source. No data moat is cited.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent is reported to have copied it. Springshare acquired the platform assets in October 2025.

market_need_then: EdSurge 2018 describes students and graduates lacking guidance for tech job searches, and the pay after hire model targeted people who could not pay upfront. Traction later included a $9M Series A in 2021.

branding.domain_note: Operated at pathrise.com; the domain returned 403 and later a directory said it was down.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as YC for your career per the YC page tagline

branding.brand_signature: Tagline YC for your career and the no job, no pay promise
branding.community_and_virality: A large volume of Trustpilot reviews exists, with mixed content; no merch or fan community was found.

brand_strength.rationale: Pathrise ran a content guide library and press coverage on its funding, but no source shows the brand itself driving growth.

outcome_analysis: Pathrise sold career coaching on an income share model, raised seed rounds in 2018 and 2019 and a $9M Series A in 2021 that included $3.5M of venture debt, and a Series B is reported for July 2022 without an amount. In October 2025 Springshare acquired its platform for CareerShift and the consumer mentorship program was set to end by the close of 2025, with the founders joining CareerShift. No source states why the consumer business ended, and an unverified Trustpilot post mentions lenders, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: pathrise.com returned HTTP 403 to fetch. Series B of 2022-07 rests on CB Insights and VCBacked databases only, amount not given; databases give conflicting totals from 2.7M to 29.2M, treated as unverified. The press total for the seed was 3.2M including the earlier 1.2M, so the 2019 entry may overlap, and the 2018 Leif financing agreement of up to 5M is credit capacity, not equity, seen only in a search snippet, so it is not recorded as a round. The Series A 9M is 5.5M equity plus 3.5M venture debt. Competitors named by EdSurge (OutCo, Interview Kickstart) are dated 2018-08, over a year after the batch, and Hired and Triplebyte pages are undated vendor content, so the list is empty. Evan Limanto appears only on the YC page. Directory status is Inactive, consistent with the wind down of the consumer program.
